title: Why mPharma Stopped Digitising Prescriptions and Took On the Stock
conflicts: Founding year 2013 (TechCrunch, HBS piece, Rockson's 2014 post dating the Zambian pilot to August 2013) vs 2014 (Skoll, Launch Base Africa, Quartz's 'three-year-old' in 2017); 2013 used. Original model: TechCrunch boilerplate says founded 'to manage prescription drug inventory', but Rockson's own 2014 post shows a digital prescription tool; the contemporary post is followed. Network size: 70+ outlets (2017), 243 pharmacies and clinics (2019), 300 partner pharmacies (Mar 2021), 200 community pharmacies (Jan 2022); only the dated 2017 and 2019 figures used. Savings: up to 30% in some cases (2017) vs 30-60% (Westminster 2019); conservative figure used. Pfizer loss in 2016 appears only in the HBS student piece and is omitted.
notes: Slate episode reframed: inventory management was a 2017 change of direction from the 2013 e-prescription start, so arc is change-of-direction and date 2017. The HBS source is an MBA student analysis on the HBS Digital Initiative site, attributed as such. Rockson's 2014 blog post is cited via an Internet Archive capture (mpharma.com does not load); the archive was briefly unreachable during checking, then loaded. The 2023 layoffs and 2025 CEO change rest on Launch Base Africa alone. Quote stance: complicates (Dhammapada v.19, the cowherd counting others' cows).
